title: relay-run stats counts a failed gate step with no verdict as a FAIL
lead: `relay-run stats` decides whether a gate round failed from its recorded verdict, and without one by proxy, when the next round-role lane step is an implementer fix round. A gate step closed with phase `fail` and no verdict is not counted as a FAIL unless a fix round follows. The TUI's `_gate_fail_lines` already treats such a step as a failed gate.
findings_note: s408 review 2026-10-30, later note: stats counts a gate FAIL by verdict, else by proxy (a fix round follows); a gate step closed with phase fail and no verdict is not counted unless a fix round follows
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing how verdicts are recorded; changing the proxy for `done` gate steps.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A run stopped after a failed gate (no fix round) undercounts gate FAILs in `stats`, and stats and the board disagree about the same step.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/relayrun.py`: `stats` / `_measure`. A gate step whose phase is `fail` and whose verdict is empty counts as a FAIL.
- `tests/test_relay_run.py`: a run whose last gate step failed with no verdict and no fix round after it.
- `docs/commands.md`: the `relay-run stats` row's gate rule.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - `test_RelayRunStats_GateFailPhaseNoVerdict_CountsAsFail`: a run with implementer, reviewer, and a gate step closed `--phase fail` with no verdict and nothing after it; `gates.fail` is 1. It fails today.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In the gate tally, check a recorded verdict first, then a `fail` phase, then the fix-round proxy.
2. Keep the JSON keys and order unchanged.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch.
